title: Copilot Credits

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: The page incorrectly says scopes without a Microsoft 365 spending policy cannot spend: Copilot Studio environments can continue under their Power Platform configuration. The licence-inclusion statement needs its documented conditions, and the Power Platform navigation and model-selector billing claim need correction.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits are the common unit for eligible Microsoft AI work billed by usage rather than a flat per-user fee.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing means charges are based on the work performed rather than a flat per-user fee.

claims.where: What a credit is, second paragraph
claims.claim: A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence covers most agent use by that user, without stating the conditions for that inclusion.
claims.quote: For agent flows, the "No charge" inclusion applies only to runs triggered via the "When an agent calls the flow" trigger, where the user interacting with the agent is authenticated with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
claims.fix: State that employee-facing standard-harness Copilot Studio usage is included when the agent operates using the authenticated licensed user's identity, subject to fair-use limits. For agent flows, inclusion requires the 'When an agent calls the flow' trigger; other triggers consume credits. Computer-Using Agents are excluded. Do not extend this inclusion to the separately billed Microsoft Copilot harness or Cowork. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management.

claims.where: What a credit is, second paragraph
claims.claim: Credits are mainly spent by unlicensed users and autonomous or background work.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Credits autonomous Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Read requirements-messages-management, usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits, and user-subscription-license-usage-based-billing; none establishes this distribution of credit spending.
claims.fix: Replace the claim about where credits are mainly spent with specific documented examples: metered Copilot Chat agents used by users without a Copilot licence, autonomous agent-flow triggers, and advanced experiences such as Cowork can consume credits. Avoid asserting a predominant spending population.

claims.fix: Add the additional Microsoft sources used to substantiate the page's facts: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/billing-manage-buy-credits ; https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management ; https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity ; https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/pay-as-you-go-usage-costs ; https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/copilot/copilot-hub ; https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-studio-costs . If the replacement frontier-model statement is retained, also cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/user-subscription-license-usage-based-billing . These uncited-source findings are consolidated here.

claims.where: Operating model, item 2
claims.claim: Scopes not covered by identity-based or resource-based Microsoft 365 spending policies simply cannot spend.
claims.quote: Environments that aren't linked to a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy continue under their applicable Power Platform configuration during the opt-in period.
claims.fix: Replace 'Uncovered scopes simply cannot spend' with 'Copilot Studio environments without a Microsoft 365 resource-based spending policy continue under their applicable Power Platform configuration. When a Microsoft 365 resource-based policy covers an environment, its Power Platform capacity allocation and linked billing plan no longer apply.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-studio-costs and distinguish this opt-in mechanism from access requirements for Microsoft 365 usage-based experiences.

claims.where: Operating model, item 3; Where the controls live, Microsoft 365 bullet

claims.quote: If a monthly per-user limit is configured, set the user-level notification thresholds. These notifications alert users as they approach their spending limit and can help them manage consumption before access is affected.

claims.where: Operating model, item 5
claims.claim: Agent grounding choices affect credit consumption.
claims.quote: For example, an agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 credits (10 credits for tenant graph-grounding, and two credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.where: Operating model; missing controls table
claims.claim: The operating checklist directs administrators to configure and review controls that have no corresponding structured controls rows.
claims.quote:
Decide which populations may spend (identity-based policies) and which resources have ceilings (resource-based policies).
Set alerts at policy and user level; decide who answers credit requests.
The page has no controls table.
claims.fix: Add structured controls rows for billing-method selection, identity-based spending policies, resource-based spending policies, policy and user alerts, credit-request routing, and consumption reporting. Use the documented paths and scope qualifications; research each API side before setting it to null. The legacy headings themselves do not require a finding.
